questions.q:
Given below are two statements :
Statement $I$: The electric force changes the speed of the charged particle and hence changes its kinetic energy; whereas the magnetic force does not change the kinetic energy of the charged particle.
Statement $II$: The electric force accelerates the positively charged particle perpendicular to the direction of electric field. The magnetic force accelerates the moving charged particle along the direction of magnetic field.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below :
options: Both Statement $I$ and Statement $II$ are correct.
Both Statement $I$ and Statement $II$ are incorrect.
Statement $I$ is correct but Statement $II$ is incorrect.
Statement $I$ is incorrect but Statement $II$ is correct.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
When a charged particle moves in an electric field, the field applies an electric& force& \left(\overset{→}{F} = q\overset{→}{E}\right)$ along the field, so work done by electric field is non-zero resulting in accelerated motion,~thus kinetic energy changes.

When a particle moves in a uniform magnetic field, the force due to magnetic field on it is perpendicular to its velocity, as~force ~ \left(\overset{→}{F} = q\overset{→}{v} \times \overset{→}{B}\right)$.
Since the magnetic field is constant, so force is constant. So, its direction of velocity constantly changes, but magnitude of velocity remains same.~Hence, kinetic energy also does not change.

~Electric field accelerates the particle in the direction of field \left(\overset{→}{F} = q\overset{→}{E} = m\overset{→}{a}\right)$and magnetic field accelerates the particle perpendicular to the field~ \left(\overset{→}{F} = q\overset{→}{v} \times \overset{→}{B} = m\overset{→}{a}\right)$.

At $t = 0$ , a positively charged particle is at the point \left($x, y, z\right) =  \left($0, 0, \dfrac{\pi}{k}\right) .$If its instantaneous velocity at \left($t = 0\right)$ is ${v}_{0}\overset{^}{k}$ , the force acting on it due to the wave is:$

questions.solution:
Force due to electric field is in direction $– \dfrac{\left(\overset{^}{i} + \overset{^}{j}\right)}{\sqrt{2}}{E}_{0}$
Force due to magnetic filed is in direction $q \left(\overset{→}{v} \times \overset{→}{B}\right)$ and \overset{→}{v} | | \overset{^}{k}$
$∴$ it is parallel to $\overset{→}{E}$
$∴$ net force is antiparallel to $\dfrac{\left(\overset{^}{i} + \overset{^}{j}\right)}{\sqrt{2}} .

questions.q:
An electron is allowed to move with constant velocity along the axis of current carrying straight solenoid.
(A) The electron will experience magnetic force along the axis of the solenoid.
(B) The electron will not experience magnetic force.
(C) The electron will continue to move along the axis of the solenoid.
(D) The electron will be accelerated along the axis of the solenoid.
(E) The electron will follow parabolic path-inside the solenoid.
Choose the correct answer from the option given below:
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
The Lorentz force is given by& $\overset{→}{F} = q ( \overset{→}{v} \times \overset{→}{B} ) = qvBsin\theta\overset{^}{n}$. The angle~$\theta = 0 °$. Hence the force experienced is zero.

Thus, the electron will not experience any magnetic force and the electron will continue to move along the axis.

questions.q:
The current sensitivity of a galvanometer can be increased by :
(A) decreasing the number of turns
(B) increasing the magnetic field
(C) decreasing the area of the coil
(D) decreasing the torsional constant of the spring

Choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below :
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
The current in the galvanometer is calculated by& $i = \left(\dfrac{K}{NAB}\right)\theta$.

Therefore, the sensitivity of the galvanometer,

$\dfrac{d\theta}{di} = \dfrac{NAB}{K}$

Hence, only options B and D are correct.

questions.q: A long straight wire of circular cross-section (radius $a$) is carrying steady current $I .$ The current $I$ is uniformly distributed across this cross-section. The magnetic field is
options: inversely& proportional to& $r$~in~the~region $r < a$~and uniform throughout in the region~$r > a$
directly proportional to& $r$~in the region~$r < a$~and inversely proportional to~$r$~in the region~$r > a$
Zero in the region& $r < a$~and inversely proportional to~$r$~in the region~$r > a$
uniform in the region& $r < a$~and inversely proportional to distance~$r$~from the axis, in the region~$r > a$
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
The formula to calculate the magnetic field inside the conducting wire is given by

${B}_{in } = \dfrac{{μ}_{0}Jr}{2} . . . ( 1 )$

The formula to calculate the magnetic field outside the conducting wire is given by

${B}_{out } = \dfrac{{μ}_{0}Ja^{2}}{2r} . . . ( 2 )$

From equation (1), it can be concluded that the magnetic field is directly proportional to the& radial distance inside the wire, whereas from equation (2), it can be concluded that the magnetic field is inversely proportional to the& radial distance outside the wire.

questions.q:
Two long parallel conductors ${S}_{1}$~and ${S}_{2}$ are separated by a distance $10$ cm and carrying currents of $4A$ and $2A$ respectively. The conductors are placed along $x$-axis in $X - Y$ plane. There is a point $P$ located between the conductors (as shown in figure).
A charge particle of $3\pi$ coulomb is passing through the point $P$ with velocity $\overset{→}{v} = \left(2\overset{^}{i} + 3\overset{^}{j}\right)ms^{- 1}$; where $\overset{^}{i}$ & $\overset{^}{j}$ represents unit vector along $x$~& $y$axis respectively.
The force acting on the charge particle is $4\pi \times {10}^{- 5}\left(- x\overset{^}{i} + 2\overset{^}{j}\right)N$. The value of $x$ is&
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
$

Net magnetic field at& $P$~is~${B}_{Net} = \left(\dfrac{{μ}_{0} \times {i}_{1}}{2\pi{r}_{1}} - \dfrac{{μ}_{0}{i}_{2}}{2\pi{r}_{2}}\right) \left(- \overset{^}{k}\right)

${B}_{Net} = $\dfrac{{μ}_{0}4}{2\pi \times \dfrac{4}{100}} - \dfrac{{μ}_{0}2}{2\pi \times \dfrac{6}{100}}

=\dfrac{\mu0}{π} \times$100 \left[\dfrac{1}{2} - \dfrac{1}{6}\right]$

$= \dfrac{\mu0}{π} \times100 \left[\dfrac{4}{2 \times 6}\right]

=\dfrac{{μ}_{0} \times 100}{3\pi} \left(- \overset{^}{k}\right)$

So, force acting on charge particle is$\overset{→}{F} = q\left(\overset{→}{v} \times \overset{→}{B}\right) ==3\pi \left[$2\overset{^}{i} + 3\overset{^}{j}\right]\dfrac{{μ}_{0} \times 100}{3\pi} \left(- \overset{^}{k}\right)$

=4\pi \times {10}^{- 7} \left[2\overset{^}{i} + 3\overset{^}{j}\right]\$times100 \left(- \overset{^}{k}\right)$

$= 4\pi \times {10}^{- 5} \left[2\overset{^}{j} - 3\overset{^}{i}\right]$

$∴ x = 3$

$

questions.q: A square loop of area $25{cm}^{2}$ has a resistance of $10Ω$. The loop is placed in uniform magnetic field of magnitude $40 . 0T$. The plane of loop is perpendicular to the magnetic field. The work done in pulling the loop out of the magnetic field slowly and uniformly in $1 . 0$ sec, will be
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
As& $l^{2} = 25{cm}^{2}$, then~$l = 5cm = 0 . 05m$.

Given:~$t = 1s$

Velocity of the square loop,~$v = \dfrac{0 . 05}{1} = 0 . 05ms^{- 1}$.

Induced current,

$i = \dfrac{V}{R} = \dfrac{Blv}{R} = \dfrac{40 \times 0 . 05 \times 0 . 05}{10} = 0 . 01A$

Now force acting on the side of the square loop,~$F = Bil = 40 \times 0 . 01 \times 0 . 05$

$⇒ F = 0 . 02N$

Therefore, work done

$W = Fl = 0 . 02 \times l = 0 . 02 \times 0 . 05$

$⇒ W = 1 \times {10}^{- 3}J$

questions.q: A long solenoid carrying a current produces a magnetic field $B$ along its axis. If the current is doubled and the number of turns per $cm$ is halved, the new value of magnetic field will be equal to
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Magnetic field due to long solenoid along its axis is given as,

$B = {μ}_{0}nI$,~where~$n$~is~the~number of turns in the solenoid per unit length,~$I$~is current in the solenoid and~${μ}_{0}$~is a constant called the permeability of free space.

$⇒ \dfrac{B1}{{B}_{2}} = \dfrac{{n}_{1}{I}_{1}}{{n}_{2}{I}_{2}}$

According to the question,~${n}_{2} = \dfrac{n1}{2}\text{and}{I}_{2} = 2{I}_{1}$

$⇒ \dfrac{B}{B2} = {n}_{1}\left(\dfrac{n1}{2}\right) \times \dfrac{I1}{2{I}_{1}} ⇒ {B}_{2} = B$; means, the& magnetic field remains the same.

questions.q:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: If the number of turns in the coil of a moving coil galvanometer is doubled then the current sensitivity becomes double.

Statement II: Increasing current sensitivity of a moving coil galvanometer by only increasing the number of turns in the coil will also increase its voltage sensitivity in the same ratio

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: Statement $I$ is true but Statement $II$ is false
Statement $I$ is false but Statement $II$ is true
Both Statement $I$ and Statement $II$& are false
Both Statement $I$ and Statement $II$ are true
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
For a moving coil galvanometer,&

\left(NiAB\right) = k\theta$

The current sensitivity is given by~

${S}_{i} = \dfrac{NAB}{k}$

So, if~$N$~is doubled then, the current sensitivity is also doubled.

The voltage is given by~

$V = \left(\dfrac{BNA}{Rk}\right)\theta$

The voltage sensitivity is given by

${S}_{v} = \left(\dfrac{NAB}{kR}\right)

As,~$N$~is increased,~$R$~also increases. So, the voltage sensitivity does not change as~$\dfrac{N}{R}$& remains constant.

A magnetic field is passing through the $x-y$ plane and expressed as $\vec{B}=B_0(1+4 x) \hat{k}$, where $B_0=5 \mathrm{~T}$. The net magnetic force experienced by the loop is _______ $\mathrm{N}$.

questions.q:
Two identical circular wires of radius $20$ cm and carrying current $\sqrt{2}A$ are placed in perpendicular~planes as shown in figure. The net magnetic field at the centre of the circular wires is________ \times {10}^{- 8}T .$

(Take~$\pi = 3 . 14)
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
The formula to calculate the magnetic field& \left(B\right)$~at the centre of a current carrying circular loop is given by

$B = \dfrac{{μ}_{0}i}{2R} . . . ( 1 )$

where,~${μ}_{0}$~is the permeability of free space,~$i$~is the current and~$R$~is the radius of the loop.

${B}_{V}, {B}_{H}$~are the magnetic field due to the vertical and the horizontal loop, which~by magnitude are equal.

The resultant magnetic field~ \left({B}_{net}\right)$~at the centre is, then, given by

${B}_{net } = \sqrt{B^{2} + B^{2}} = \sqrt{2}B = \dfrac{\sqrt{2} \times 4\pi \times {10}^{- 7} \times \sqrt{2}}{2 \times 0 . 2}$

$= 628 \times {10}^{- 8}T$

questions.q: A coil having 100 turns, area of $5 \times 10^{-3} \mathrm{~m}^2$, carrying current of $1 \mathrm{~mA}$ is placed in uniform magnetic field of $0.20 \mathrm{~T}$ such a way that plane of coil is perpendicular to the magnetic field. The work done in turning the coil through $90^{{}^{{}^{\circ}}}$ is _______ $\mu \mathrm{J}$.

questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} & W=\Delta U=U_f-U_i \\ & W=(-\vec{\mu} . \vec{B})_f-(-\vec{\mu} . \vec{B})_i \\ & =0+(\vec{\mu} \cdot \vec{B})_i \\ & =\left(100 \times 5 \times 10^{-3} \times 1 \times 10^{-3}\right) \times 0.2 \mathrm{~J} \\ & =1 \times 10^{-4} \mathrm{~J}=100 \mu \mathrm{J}\end{aligned}$
